tooltip: Cross Hair Off - No crosshair overlay
content1: No crosshair overlay is displayed on the preview. The frame is shown clean without any aiming or centering guides.

tooltip: Perpendicular Cross Hair - Full frame cross lines with center dot
content1: Draws a full horizontal and vertical line across the entire frame, intersecting at the center with a small dot. Provides a precise center reference across the whole frame.
content2: Align your subject along either the horizontal or vertical line, or place it exactly at the center intersection point for a perfectly centered composition.
content3: Centering subjects precisely, checking camera level, aligning architectural elements, and any scene requiring strict horizontal or vertical reference lines.
content4: Use the perpendicular crosshair to check if your camera is level when shooting architecture or landscapes. Any tilt in the scene will be immediately visible against the lines.

tooltip: Circle Cross Hair - Dotted circle with center plus marker
content1: Displays a dotted circle centered on the frame with a small plus marker at the center. The circle provides a circular region of interest guide around the center of the frame.
content2: Place your subject within or along the boundary of the circle to keep it within the natural center focus zone. The plus marker confirms the exact center point.
content3: Circular framing compositions, keeping a moving subject within a defined central zone, and macro or close-up photography where precise centering matters.
content4: The dotted circle acts as a soft boundary guide rather than a hard crop line. Use it to keep your subject loosely centered while still allowing natural framing variation.

tooltip: Dot Cross Hair - Minimal plus symbol at center
content1: Displays a minimal plus symbol at the exact center of the frame. The least intrusive crosshair option, providing just enough reference without obscuring the scene.
content2: Use the plus marker as a subtle center reference point. Unlike the perpendicular crosshair it does not extend lines across the full frame, keeping the view clean.
content3: General shooting where a minimal center indicator is preferred, fast-moving subjects, and situations where the full crosshair lines would be too distracting.
content4: The dot crosshair is ideal when you need just enough center reference without the visual weight of full frame lines. Pairs well with any grid overlay for combined guidance.
